unsupported_claims: Top-level '"license": "MIT"' reads as if the whole stack is MIT. The raw README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/README.md, fetched 2026-09-18) says MIT for the repo but explicitly lists third-party components with OTHER licenses: OmniParser CC-BY-4.0 and optional 'cua-agent[omni]' includes ultralytics AGPL-3.0. The reading never flags the AGPL-3.0 optional dependency, which is a hard constraint for vendoring/reuse in a permissive codebase. Flat 'license: MIT' is misleading.

'local_maxxing_relevance' point 2: 'Cua-Bench runs lightweight webtop environments on a single CPU with no virtualization and is MIT -- plausible on the 4-core ARM box for eval/data-gen.' The quote 'Lightweight webtop environments (single CPU, no virtualization)' is verified verbatim in the HF blog (https://huggingface.co/blog/cua-ai/cua-bench, fetched 2026-09-18), but 'plausible on the 4-core ARM box' is an inference with ZERO measured run in the reading. It is tagged MEASURED while being an ESTIMATE. The reading contains no aarch64/ARM execution evidence.

The reading asserts the KiCad EDA tasks 'need a real KiCad GUI environment' (local_maxxing_relevance point 2). That is not in any source I could find and is an ESTIMATE presented inside a MEASURED-tagged bullet; it may well be true, but the reading did not measure it and did not mark it.

'trajectory_shape.C_sdk_tracing_api' is tagged 'MEASURED (from search snippet of the page; direct fetch failed)' and even says 'Treat as MEASURED-from-snippet.' A search-engine snippet is not a page read under the stage's own definition ('MEASURED (from a file/page you read)'). Self-contradictory tag; the trace_metadata/event file inventory is unverified.

The Cua Driver recording contract is cited from a THIRD-PARTY npm bundle (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@amaster.ai/pi-computer-use@0.1.3/bin/darwin-x64/.../RECORDING.md), not the official trycua/cua repo. The content checks out verbatim (I re-fetched it 2026-09-18) but the reading never flags that it is an unofficial repackaged copy of a darwin-x64 app bundle -- a provenance risk for a claim about the official recording format.

The reading's 'one_line' says the stack is 'MIT' and 'provides the computer and the evaluation/training harness, not a model' -- the second half is supported (README: 'You bring the agent and model. Cua provides the computer and automation tools.'), but the first half repeats the license overstatement above.

The reading presents the report's root-cause split ('40% planning/policy, 22% perception, 19% navigation inefficiency, 11% domain knowledge, 8% tool-API') as fact. Verified verbatim in the report (https://cua.ai/cuabench/report, fetched 2026-09-18). Not an error -- but the same report separately says 'about 80% of error-mode mentions landed in planning, perception, or navigation inefficiency'; the reading does not note that the report mixes two different aggregations (error-mode mentions vs root-cause category share) in adjacent paragraphs.
errors_found: HARD STAGE ERROR (the reason read:cua-readme failed): the payload does not match the workflow's required read schema in extensions/agi/workflows/trove-survey.json. Required keys are [source, summary, key_facts, reusable_assets, failures_and_lessons, hypothesis_seeds, open_questions]. The file's actual keys are [stage, role, town, date_read, primary_source_url, license, one_line, cua_bench, model_scores, trajectory_shape, releases_or_trains_model, local_maxxing_relevance, sources_read, read_only_statement]. ZERO of the 7 required keys are present. This is exactly the 'no schema-valid JSON and no complete result_file' failure recorded in .agi/sessions/workflows/trove-cua.log (2026-09-18) and is why read:cua-readme failed twice.

Wrong result_file path: the stage declares result_file '{scratch}/read-{key}.json' where scratch resolves to .agi/context/local-maxxing/troves/2026-09-19-cua/ (where read-cua-docs.json and read-typesafe-changelog.json actually landed). The reader wrote /read-cua-readme.json and /tmp/read-cua-readme.json instead. Even a schema-valid payload would not have been collected from the declared location.

trajectory_shape.A_cua_bench_trace.row_fields lists 4 fields [trajectory_id, event_name, data_json, data_images]. The actual dataset produced by cua-bench v0.2.11 on this box has 5: [event_name, data_json, data_images, trajectory_id, timestamp] -- MEASURED in .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trace_excerpt.json ('dataset_features'). The 'timestamp' field is omitted. (The 4-field list is faithful to the main-branch traces.py the reader read, so this is an incompleteness, not a fabrication.)

trajectory_shape.A_cua_bench_trace.event_names claims 'agent_step'. The installed cua-bench v0.2.11 trace uses 'step:before' and 'step:after' -- MEASURED in .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trace_excerpt.json. The main-branch traces.py (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/trainer/off_policy/tinker/traces.py, fetched 2026-09-18) does use 'agent_step' (by_event.get('agent_step')), so the reading is faithful to main but contradicts the measured on-box artefact. Version drift between main and the released package is real and unflagged -- the most consequential error in the reading.

Step-budget inconsistency unflagged: the leaderboard says '200-step budget' (https://cuabench.ai/leaderboard), while the technical report says 'The point was to make the 150-step budget genuinely generous' and 'Every full pass finished under 150 turns' (https://cua.ai/cuabench/report). The reading quotes 200 from the leaderboard and treats 150 only as a turn count, never noting the 200-vs-150 discrepancy between the two official pages.

Cohort-size inconsistency unflagged: the leaderboard lists 10 models; the report TL;DR says it 'ran seven frontier computer-use agents' and names 7. Three leaderboard entries (Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Muse Spark 1.1) do not appear in the report cohort list. The reading reproduces both but does not reconcile them.

No source is pinned to a commit SHA or archived: every GitHub/docs URL is 'main' or live. Given the demonstrated event_name drift between main and v0.2.11, all trajectory-format claims are unpinned and can silently change. The reading's date stamp ('2026-09-18') is the only provenance.
Minor: model_scores.the_requested_0_267_line names only Gemini 3.5 Flash at 0.267; Claude Fable 5 (rank 1) also has mean_reward 0.267. The reading does not note the tie.
missing_angles: The reading ignored the local measured artefact already in the repo: .agi/context/local-maxxing/cua/cua_trace_excerpt.json + cua_trajectory_mapping.md -- a real cua-bench v0.2.11 simulated 'first-task' run on ARM4C headless, reward 1.0, with a field-by-field jev acts_replay mapping. NOTE FOR FAIRNESS: those files are mtime 2026-09-18 19:28 EDT, one hour AFTER this reading was written (18:29 EDT), so the reader could not have used them. But the critique must record that the reading's own open question ('does the simulated provider run on aarch64 ARM with no VM/Docker?') is now answered MEASURED locally, and its relevance inference is superseded.

No cross-check of the on-disk dataset schema against the main-branch traces.py the reading read. The 'agent_step' vs 'step:before/after' drift and the missing 'timestamp' field would have been caught by one grep of the local trace excerpt.

No mention of the README's own strongest headless evidence: 'Start with a simulated task that requires no VM, Docker, or model API key' and the install path `uv tool install 'cua-bench[browser]'` + `playwright install chromium` (verified in raw README 2026-09-18). The reading leaned on the HF blog for the $0/headless claim instead of the primary README line.
No flag of the AGPL-3.0 ultralytics optional extra / OmniParser CC-BY-4.0 third-party licenses (README), a real reuse risk for the town.
No version/commit pinning anywhere; no archive.org/wayback citation for any number. For a trove whose output is 'reusable assets', that is a reproducibility gap.

No local feasibility numbers the town actually needs: per-task wall time, disk footprint of cua-bench[browser]+chromium, RAM headroom on the 4-core ARM box. The reading gives effort estimates nowhere and cost nowhere (unlike the sibling read-cua-docs.json, which at least gave ESTIMATE costs).

The reading never states that the Cua-Bench EDA leaderboard is a single-domain (EDA/KiCad), v1-only suite, so 'computer-use mastery' generalisation from 6/25 is weak. (It does note v1 is EDA/KiCad only in cua_bench.task_set, but not the generalisation caveat.)

No attempt to locate the owner's cited 'open model beats closed-source' claim in the pages it read. The sibling read-cua-docs.json explicitly answers this ('NO open-weight model appears in the v1 EDA leaderboard'), and this reading's leaderboard reproduction confirms it -- but the reading never draws the conclusion, leaving the owner's premise unaddressed in the artefact of record.
strongest_seed: The reading has NO hypothesis_seeds array (schema violation), so no seed can be judged as written. Strongest supported direction it actually documents: the trajectory/typed-acts reuse direction -- Cua-Bench traces.py Step/Episode dataclasses and the Cua Driver turn-NNNNN folder contract are both verified verbatim against primary sources, are pure-Python/JSON, cost $0 and are CPU-cheap, and the local measured mapping (cua_trajectory_mapping.md) already shows a closed set of 12 action classes. Claim to test: the Cua-Bench trace schema maps onto .agi/context/local-maxxing/typesafe/acts_replay.jsonl with a <=20-line adapter; falsifier: action.json is free-text/screenshot-only or the mapping loses action type/target/args/observation.
weakest_seed: Weakest supported direction: the 'local-maxxing relevance' inference that Cua-Bench (and the KiCad EDA suite specifically) is runnable on the 4-core ARM box for eval/data-gen. It is an ESTIMATE presented under a MEASURED tag, backed by zero measured run in the reading, and the report's own evidence (dense KiCad GUI, 25 long-horizon EDA tasks, 0/16 from-scratch builds, 81% of failures planning/perception/navigation) makes it the highest-cost, lowest-knowledge-per-token target on the list. If a tiny model is to be tested at all, the report's own per-task data says only single-value edits are plausible, which the reading never states as a measured bound.
